subject: Renewal proposal: flexible annualization + onboarding credits for Neptune Analytics

Subject: Renewal proposal: flexible annualization + onboarding credits for Neptune Analytics

Hi Raj —

Great speaking last week. Based on usage trends and the scaling you projected for Q1–Q3 next year, attached is a proposed renewal structure that aims to balance predictability for Neptune with flexibility during your product onboarding window. High-level summary: 

- 24-month base term (option to extend to 36 months at a locked rate)
- Annualized commit (billing monthly) with an onboarding credit applied in month 1 and month 2 to offset integration volume
- Surge bucket: 20% burst alloc that can be consumed at a blended overage rate (tokens) with an option to convert to committed capacity mid-term
- Auto-renew by default at current rates unless Neptune provides a 60-day opt-out notice; we can negotiate different opt-out windows for multi-year locks
- SLA addendum for dedicated capacity (if you choose reserved GPUs) with a credit schedule for missed p99 latency targets

Attachments: Neptune_TermSheet_v2.pdf (term sheet) and Neptune_Onboarding_Playbook.xlsx (onboarding milestones + credits timeline).

Next steps I recommend: 1) Review term sheet, 2) Marcus to confirm provisioning timeline for reserved pools, 3) your procurement to confirm billing cadence (monthly invoicing vs annual prepay).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk through. Are you available Thu 11/4 or Fri 11/5?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Kimberly —

Thanks for the thorough draft. A few clarifying questions before we loop procurement in formally: 

1) Can you clarify how the onboarding credit offsets are applied? Is it a dollar credit on the first two invoices or token credit that consumes before overage?
2) For the surge bucket: what is the overage rate and is there any minimum notice before we convert surge into a committed increase?
3) We like the annualized commit idea, but procurement prefers simpler annual invoicing for budgeting. Would Redwood do annual invoicing for the annualized commit (i.e., bill once a year) if we commit to 36 months?

Elena and I are generally aligned that an initial protected burst during onboarding is critical — we'll want the on-call escalation path documented in the SLA.

Can you also confirm the timeline to get reserved capacity provisioned (if we take it) and whether any lead time or quota needs to be reserved on our cloud account?

-Raj
VP Product, Neptune Analytics

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 11:38 AM Raj Patel <raj@neptune-analytics.com> wrote:
> Kimberly —
> 
> Thanks for the thorough draft. A few clarifying questions before we loop procurement in formally: 
> 
> 1) Can you clarify how the onboarding credit offsets are applied? Is it a dollar credit on the first two invoices or token credit that consumes before overage?
> 2) For the surge bucket: what is the overage rate and is there any minimum notice before we convert surge into a committed increase?
> 3) We like the annualized commit idea, but procurement prefers simpler annual invoicing for budgeting. Would Redwood do annual invoicing for the annualized commit (i.e., bill once a year) if we commit to 36 months?

Thanks for flagging — answers inline below.

1) Onboarding credit: It's a token-based credit that is applied as a pre-pay deduction before any overage consumption. Practically: month 1 and month 2 invoice will show token consumption first drawn from the credit line, then from committed units, then from overage. We'll also surface the credit consumption detail on the invoice.

2) Surge bucket & conversion: the proposed overage rate in the term sheet is $0.0025 per 1k tokens (blended), with a 14-day minimum notice to convert surge into committed capacity (to allow scheduling on GPU pools). We can accelerate conversion with a 72-hour emergency adjust if you pay the surge conversion fee (one-time). If you'd prefer automatic conversion after sustained usage (e.g., 7 days >80% surge utilization), we can add that as an automated policy.

3) Annual invoicing: yes — for 36-month locked commitments we can offer annual invoicing (one invoice per 12 months). To keep unit economics predictable we lock rates for the full 36 months and include a single annual invoice schedule in the SOW.

Marcus — can you confirm provisioning lead time for reserved pools and whether we need any quotas set on Neptune's cloud account?

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Quick provisioning note from infra: reserved capacity lead time is typically 10 business days once the purchase is confirmed and the reserved pool config is approved. For a 36-month reserved pool we recommend reserving at least 2 extra GPU slots as buffer for the onboarding burst.

Quota: Neptune will need to ensure the cloud project has the required GPU quota (we'll provide the exact SKU list once the SOW is signed). If you want us to open the quota request with your cloud account team, we can do that as part of the onboarding checklist.

Elena/Procurement — if the above aligns, I'll attach a short provisioning checklist and turn-key timeline. Kimberly — happy to be on the kickoff call to walk infra runbook and escalation matrix.

Best,
